name: realtimex-mailkeeper
description: AI-guided inbox maintenance: verify accounts, preview safely, then choose whether to schedule promoted rules.

api_routes.description: Read a workspace MailKeeper profile, readiness state, promoted rules, and last run summary.
List Himalaya accounts from the configured email config as select options for EMAIL_ACCOUNTS. Never returns hosts or secrets.
Record a finite cleanup run receipt (actions taken, proposals, urgent items), including after workspace deactivation.
Promote a proposed rule so the heartbeat may execute it unattended. Human-only.
Demote a promoted rule back to proposal. Human-only.
Reverse every action recorded in one run receipt by UID.
Explicitly re-provision the profile-owned thread, contract file, and managed heartbeat task.

summary.title: Set up MailKeeper
summary.description: Install email tools, connect accounts privately, verify settings, and run your first report-only preview.

dependencies.title: Email via Himalaya
dependencies.description: Read IMAP mail through the shared email configuration.
dependencies.doctorDescription: Check the real binary, install with approval, and configure non-secret IMAP settings.

editor.taskPrompt: Help me set up MailKeeper for this workspace, starting with my email tools and account connection. Keep the first inbox preview report-only.
editor.initialContent:
# MailKeeper setup

Email tools → Account connection → MailKeeper settings → Prepare → First preview → Schedule

Connection checks and preparation are verified by the plugin. Saving this guide does not verify or schedule anything.
editor.prompt: Begin by saying: I will check your email setup, help you connect an account, and prepare your first preview. Enter passwords only in the private credential window when prompted. The first preview makes no mailbox changes. Show the setup checklist with observed completed, active, awaiting action or failed states: Email tools, Account connection, MailKeeper settings, Prepare MailKeeper, First preview, Schedule. Guide the user through MailKeeper setup in this exact workspace. Use node .agents/skills/mailbox-cleanup/scripts/mailkeeper-setup.js status to inspect current state and the shared email target revision. Check command -v himalaya, himalaya --version, and himalaya --help. For a missing CLI, propose the supported platform install command and request ordinary command approval; verify the actual binary after installation. Never run account doctor --fix automatically. Ask only for non-secret provider/IMAP details. Offer reuse of existing account names before adding an account. For macOS password accounts, use the setup helper account command with JSON fields name,email,displayName,host,port,encryption,login,revision; an environment target requires explicit confirmOverride. The host preserves unrelated accounts, defaults, SMTP and BizOps sections. Never read raw shared TOML into the AI transcript, write credentials, or ask for passwords/tokens/app passwords. Direct the user to the workspace plugin card private credential panel for native Keychain Access entry, then Check again. Other platforms and unsupported auth references remain pending; do not invent OAuth or vault integration. Have the user choose Email accounts, Maintenance agent, optional model, and report-only mode using Configure, or save validated non-secret workspace fields using the helper configure command. The host-selected agent must be installed; do not change the workspace default agent. Run helper check to start resumable preparation; status reads are cached and do not probe. Explain typed blockers and resume the same operation. Ready requires all selected accounts and readback of the maintenance thread, MAILBOX.md, rules and disabled managed task. Use the card Preview inbox action with explicit human confirmation. It performs a finite five-page-per-account INBOX report-only preview and writes a receipt, even if stored MODE is higher. Never move, delete, send, add folders, promote rules, or enable scheduling during setup. Scheduling is a separate human action on the card after successful verification. Preserve existing accounts, rules, MAILBOX.md, receipts and scheduler pause/cadence. Do not claim successful setup or preview from AI prose; check the stored plugin status and receipt.

configSchema.label: Mode ceiling
configSchema.description: Highest mode any workspace may use. Set once, globally.

options.label: Label only (move to Auto/* folders, never leave the inbox)

configSchema.label: Auto folder prefix
configSchema.description: Folder prefix for audit-trail moves, e.g. Auto/Newsletters.

configSchema.label: Protected sender domains
configSchema.description: Sender domains no rule may ever touch. Applies to every workspace.

configSchema.label: Run receipt retention (days)
configSchema.description: How long run receipts (and undo) are kept.

configSchema.label: Email accounts
configSchema.description: Accounts this workspace keeps clean. Sourced from the BizOps Himalaya config; each gets its own snapshot and Auto/* folders.

configSchema.label: Mode
configSchema.description: What the heartbeat may do unattended. Cannot exceed the global mode ceiling.

configSchema.label: Heartbeat cadence
configSchema.description: How often the maintenance run happens. Follows this workspace's heartbeat active hours and pause state.

configSchema.label: Age threshold (days)
configSchema.description: Messages older than this qualify for the age pass.

configSchema.label: Aggressiveness
configSchema.description: Which passes may be promoted. See MAILBOX.md for the pass list per level.

configSchema.label: VIP senders
configSchema.description: Addresses or domains that are never touched. Seeds MAILBOX.md.

configSchema.label: Maintenance agent
configSchema.description: Terminal agent that runs the maintenance task.

configSchema.label: Model
configSchema.description: Optional. Empty means the agent's default model.

configSchema.label: Scheduled maintenance
configSchema.description: Off for a new workspace. Existing maintenance intent is migrated once. Setup and first preview do not enable scheduling.
